thread:
incident-bot: Pager fired for service=inference-gateway env=staging severity=critical — 5xx spike detected during staged rollout v3.7.1. metric: gateway.5xx_rate > 5% for 2m. paging: pagerduty 🔔

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident #INC-2026-439 created, escalation policy: infra-oncall. Initial alert: gateway 5xx rate 6.8% (p99 latency stable).

SRE Oncall: Acking on behalf of infra-oncall — I'm on it. Starting triage now.

Elias Park: saw the alert. Quick question — is this traffic only to the new variant? I see traffic split 20% -> v3.7.1, 80% -> v3.6.9 per rollout policy.

Maya Patel: yes confirmed, new variant is staged (traffic=20%). Logs show 502/503 from runtime with kv-cache timeouts. Possible memoria alloc path? grabbing recent logs.

SRE Oncall: paste of recent error tail:
```
2026-03-14T20:04:02Z inference-gateway[router] ERROR request_id=abcd1234 downstream=embedder timeout_ms=1500 status=502
2026-03-14T20:04:03Z runtime-0 WARN kvcache miss ratio increased from 0.02 -> 0.35
2026-03-14T20:04:04Z runtime-0 ERROR OOM prevention triggered, falling back to baseline kernels
```

Elias Park: interesting — OOM prevention + kvcache thrash. Could be new quant kernels in v3.7.1. Rolling back kernels might help but quicker is to divert traffic.

Priya Singh: tagging product & support. @Support Ops can you start an incident notification for customers on staging/private preview? We should provide ETA and mitigation steps. :warning:

Support Ops: Will do. Drafting message for affected partners now, will post in #customer-impact once we have rollback plan.

SRE Oncall: Mitigation options on the table:
- divert traffic back to v3.6.9 (fastest)
- scale up runtime pool for v3.7.1 (buy time)
- revert rollout completely (if rollback validated)

Elias Park: I can trigger a traffic diversion to 0% -> v3.7.1 and 100% -> v3.6.9 via rollout controller. Command: 
```bash
redwoodctl rollout set inference-gateway --variant v3.6.9 --traffic 100 --namespace staging
```

Maya Patel: I can attempt a canary patch to disable the new kernel flag (quant fallback) but that might require a deploy and will take longer. Recommend diversion + monitor.

Priya Singh: Agreed. Do diversion now, then decide if we want to revert the release entirely. We need timeline for customer impact assessment. How many requests impacted?

SRE Oncall: Querying telemetry: current 5xx during spike ~ 2.4k/min across staging; of those, ~85% routed to v3.7.1. Estimating % of total customers in staging impacted ~ 4% of staging traffic.

Elias Park: Executing diversion now (will announce when done).

SRE Oncall: Command executed: 
```
> redwoodctl rollout set inference-gateway --variant v3.6.9 --traffic 100 --namespace staging
Applied rollout change: v3.7.1 traffic -> 0% (draining), v3.6.9 -> 100%
```

incident-bot: Automated note: rollout change detected by controller at 2026-03-14T20:06:12Z — alert suppression applied for associated 5xx_alert rule for 3m.

Maya Patel: I'm seeing error rate drop already, 5xx down from 6.8% -> 1.2% in the last 90s. Good signal.

SRE Oncall: Confirming drain: v3.7.1 pods are terminating gracefully, no new traffic. Starting to collect post-mitigation metrics for 15m window.

Priya Singh: Good. Do we want to open a rollback ticket for v3.7.1 from the release owner? If metrics stable we can mark release as paused and create follow-up investigation.

Elias Park: I'll create a rollback PR to revert the rollout in the release controller and add a postmortem ticket.

Support Ops: Customer message ready — sending to #customer-impact and emailing partners on staging preview: short note, apologizing and noting mitigation (traffic diverted, no further action required).

incident-bot: PagerDuty incident updated: status=acknowledged, note: traffic diversion executed.

Priya Singh: For exec / CS: initial impact estimate = small but visible on staging partner orgs only. No production customers affected. We should still run an RCA because this affects kernel selection.

Elias Park: Adding immediate next steps in ticket:
- capture runtime heap/kvcache profiles for v3.7.1 pods (pre-drain logs preserved)
- run regression test suite with quant kernels + OOM stress harness
- coordinate with runtime/infra to identify kernel change that caused regression

Maya Patel: I'll keep an eye on logs and try the quick kernel toggle on a single node in a sandbox cluster for repro.

SRE Oncall: Monitoring window in progress — will update in 5m. If stable, we will resolve the PagerDuty incident as mitigated and convert to postmortem tasking.

(5 minutes pass)

SRE Oncall: 5m update: 5xx rate steady at 0.8%, p95 latency unchanged. No new pages during suppression window.

incident-bot: PagerDuty incident #INC-2026-439 status changed to resolved by infra-oncall at 2026-03-14T20:12:30Z — follow-ups moved to ticket RED-5342 (deploy regression: v3.7.1 kernels).

Priya Singh: Thanks team. Elias, Maya — please own the follow-ups and loop in runtime kernel lead. I'll schedule a postmortem and invite product and support.

Elias Park: On it. Closing thread here but will post status updates in RED-5342.

Support Ops: Customer messages sent and CSMs notified. No incoming escalations so far. :white_check_mark:

Maya Patel: saved debug bundle and logs to s3://redwood-debug/RED-5342/2026-03-14/ — includes KV cache histograms and kernel traces.

SRE Oncall: Handing off to daytime rotation. If anything re-escalates, page infra-oncall again.

incident-bot: Thread archived.
